datasets.title: Millennium Simulation
datasets.description: A 500 Mpc/h cube of simulated galaxies, as UniverseVR showed it
datasets.credit: Millennium Simulation, Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics (Springel et al. 2005; Lemson & Virgo Consortium 2006), as packaged in UniverseVR by Markus Lipp

datasets.title: CfA1 survey
datasets.description: The first CfA redshift survey: the northern sky to m ≈ 14.5, 1977–82
datasets.credit: CfA Redshift Survey (Davis, Huchra, Latham & Tonry 1982; Huchra et al. 1983), via the CfA Redshift Catalog (ZCAT)

datasets.title: CfA2 survey
datasets.description: The second CfA survey, which found the Great Wall: to m ≈ 15.5, 1985–95
datasets.credit: CfA2 Redshift Survey (Geller & Huchra 1989; Huchra et al. 1990, 1995), via the CfA Redshift Catalog (ZCAT)

datasets.title: 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey
datasets.description: Two thin wedges of sky to z ≈ 0.3, 1997–2002
datasets.credit: 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey final data release (Colless et al. 2001, 2003), Anglo-Australian Observatory

datasets.title: SDSS main galaxy sample
datasets.description: A sixth of the Sloan survey’s flux-limited galaxies (r < 17.77) to z ≈ 0.3, 2000–08
datasets.credit: Sloan Digital Sky Survey DR17 (Abdurro’uf et al. 2022), main galaxy sample (Strauss et al. 2002); SDSS is funded by the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, the participating institutions and the US DOE Office of Science

datasets.title: SDSS BOSS / eBOSS
datasets.description: Luminous red and emission-line galaxies from BOSS and eBOSS, out to z ≈ 1.1, 2009–19
datasets.credit: Sloan Digital Sky Survey DR17 (Abdurro’uf et al. 2022): BOSS (Dawson et al. 2013) and eBOSS (Dawson et al. 2016); SDSS is funded by the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, the participating institutions and the US DOE Office of Science

datasets.title: DESI DR1
datasets.description: Bright, luminous red and emission-line galaxies from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, out to z ≈ 1.6, 2021–22
datasets.credit: DESI Data Release 1 (DESI Collaboration 2025), photometry from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys DR9, via NOIRLab’s Astro Data Lab; DESI is supported by the US DOE Office of Science and the participating institutions
